stories.headline: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Afghanistan: NCS
stories.title: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Afghanistan: NCS
stories.summary: Kabul , October 1 : An earthquake of magnitude 5.3 struck Afghanistan on Thursday morning, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said. According to the NCS, the earthquake occurred at 6:59:20 am IST at a depth of 126 km. In a post shared on X, the NCS said, "EQ of M: 5.3, On: 01/10/2026 06:59:20 IST, Lat: 35.981 N, Long: 68.700 E, Depth: 126 Km, Location: Afghanistan." The NCS located the earthquake at latitude 35.981 North and longitude 68.700 East, around 165 km NNW of Kabul. Further details are awaited.

stories.headline: Agricultural information centre launched under Palasbari LAC in Kamrup district
stories.title: Agricultural information centre launched under Palasbari LAC in Kamrup district
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: AZARA: An Agricultural Technology Information Centre was inaugurated at the premises of the Swargiya Basudev Library at Bakarapar under the Palasbari LAC in Kamrup district on Tuesday.
The centre has been established through the initiative of six final-year students of the College of Horticulture and Agricultural Sciences, Nalbari, under Assam Agricultural University.
It was formally inaugurated by Rukun Rabha, President of the Sayan-Rani Development Block.

Addressing the gathering as a distinguished guest, Dr Samiran Pathak, scientist at the Horticultural Research Centre, Kahikuchi, said that the information centre should serve as a bridge between farmers and agricultural scientists, enabling farmers to seek scientific assistance in resolving complex problems related to agriculture.

The centre has been established through the efforts of six students of Assam Agricultural University - Nayanjyoti Kalita, Tadab Tana, Jinjit Pegu, Achik Iqbal, Abdul Aziz Majumdar, and Prabaljyoti Barman.

stories.headline: UP Rajya Sabha election 2026: Will the 10th seat be decided by cross-voting? Here's what we know
stories.title: UP Rajya Sabha election 2026: Will the 10th seat be decided by cross-voting? Here's what we know
stories.summary: With both the SP and BJP short of the numbers for their extra seats, every vote has become critical.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With the contest for the 10th Rajya Sabha seat turning into a tense test of numbers and nerves, both the ruling side and the Opposition are keeping a close watch on each other’s MLAs amid the possibility of cross-voting.
The Samajwadi Party has claimed that some NDA legislators are in touch with it and may cross-vote if they are assured of tickets, Aaj Tak reported, citing sources.

The contest for the 10th seat is being seen as dependent on cross-voting, as the Samajwadi Party does not have the numbers to win a third seat on its own, while the BJP also does not have enough strength to secure an eighth seat without support from outside its committed tally.
In this situation, some MLAs could vote against their party line and back a candidate from the other side.
The report said jailed SP MLA Ramakant Yadav will not be able to vote in the Rajya Sabha election.
With seven Assembly seats lying vacant, a maximum of 395 votes can be cast.
By this calculation, 37 votes are needed to win one Rajya Sabha seat.
After excluding the MLAs who had rebelled against the SP in the previous Rajya Sabha election, the party has 99 votes, including those of two Congress MLAs.
To win three seats, the SP needs 108 votes.
This means it needs to arrange nine additional votes for its third candidate.
The votes of two Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) MLAs, Abbas Ansari and Jagdish Narayan Rai, are being seen as likely to go to the SP.
Jagdish Narayan Rai had also voted for the SP candidate in the previous election.

stories.headline: Pakistan's information minister criticises India's decision to hold IWT in abeyance
stories.title: Pakistan's information minister criticises India's decision to hold IWT in abeyance
stories.summary: India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025, a day after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people, saying it would remain suspended until Pakistan takes credible action against cross-border terrorism
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in summary weight 50.4
article_sentences: Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Wednesday criticised India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance, saying it was a binding pact.

The IWT of 1960 is a World Bank-brokered agreement between India and Pakistan that governs the sharing of the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin, allocating the eastern rivers to India and the western rivers largely to Pakistan.

India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025, a day after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people, saying it would remain suspended until Pakistan takes credible action against cross-border terrorism.
Addressing an event organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, Tarar said that the IWT was legally binding.

He said that the treaty cannot be “unilaterally altered, revoked, rescinded or held in abeyance, for that matter, but even if there is a dispute, both the parties have to adhere to the terms and conditions of the treaty”.
The minister warned that Indian action to suspend the treaty would have global implications.
Tarar reiterated that Pakistan will continue to engage the international community and defend the country’s vital national interests.
“We are a peaceful nation, but we cannot allow India to weaponise water because it is the basic right of the 240 million people of Pakistan,” Tarar said.

stories.headline: INDIA bloc to launch nationwide campaign against CEC, SIR from October 2
stories.title: INDIA bloc to launch nationwide campaign against CEC, SIR from October 2
stories.summary: Opposition parties to move Supreme Court, hold district-level marches and seek President’s intervention over electoral roll revision and Election Commission functioning
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) announced a nationwide campaign beginning Friday (October 2, 2026) with a graded agitation plan that includes protest marches at district headquarters, public meetings, a march to the Election Commission and a joint appeal to the Chief Justice for expedited hearings in cases related to the SIR and alleged electoral “malpractices”.
The decisions were taken after a three-and-a-half-hour meeting attended by 33 leaders from 19 political parties.
Independent MP and senior Supreme Court lawyer Kapil Sibal also participated.
Mr. Sibal recommended that the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, should be legally challenged.

The legislation states that “notwithstanding other laws, no court could entertain or continue civil or criminal proceedings against a person who was or had been CEC/EC for an act, thing, or word committed, done, or spoken while discharging official duty or function,” extending a blanket immunity to the CEC.

In view of this, he suggested that legal action be taken against other Election Commission officials such as Seema Khanna, Director General (IT) at ECI, who have been instrumental in bringing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Most leaders backed the proposal.
There was, however, apprehension among some leaders about the Supreme Court’s stance.

Shiv Sena (UBT) leader and former Maharashtra Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray, who joined the meeting virtually, cited the Chief Justice of India’s observation while declining an early hearing of pleas related to the SIR in West Bengal.
The CJI had observed, “These are only by-elections.”
There was no direct reference to involving the Cockroach Janata Party.
However, leaders agreed that the bloc should engage with civil society and secular parties outside the INDIA alliance.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Rebukes UP Police Over FIR Discrepancies, Summons Officer
stories.title: Supreme Court Rebukes UP Police Over FIR Discrepancies, Summons Officer
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(September 30) criticised the Uttar Pradesh police for registering a first information report against an unknown person in a case of motorcycle theft, despite the fact that the complainant had apprehended the thief on the spot.

In a case before Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva, the complainant appeared in person and alleged that despite him informing the UP Police about the person who stole his motorcycle, the police registered an FIR and left the column for adding the name of the accused person blank.
He stated that it was only after she approached the Allahabad High Court that the police added the name of an unknown person as accused.
The complainant ultimately had to knock on the doors of the Supreme Court.
When the matter came up here, the Court had asked the UP Police to file an affidavit in this regard, which was filed by Shobit Kumar, Circle, Khurja, Bulandshahr, UP.
However, the Court found the affidavit to be "utterly uninspiring" because it clearly revealed the FIR was supplemented with the accused's name later.
Questioning how an investigating agency could break the trust of the people, Justice Kumar asked the Circle Officer to be present in the next hearing.
"We find the affidavit dated 25.09.2026 filed by Mr. Shobhit Kumar, Circle Officer, Khurja, Bulandsahr, Uttar Pradesh, to be utterly uninspiring.
The said officer shall be present before this Court on the next date of hearing to account for the same.

It would be open to him to file a better affidavit explaining as to why First Information Report No. 195/2026 was registered on 19.08.2026 against an unknown motorcycle rider when it is the admitted fact that the said motorcycle rider was apprehended at the spot.
In paragraph 6 of the aforestated affidavit, the name of the motorcycle rider is disclosed as Tushar s/o Sh.
Prempal.
